answer: The yarrow on a high ridge is never counted in one walk. So let the ledger audit unpredictably: on a random epoch, any account must re-open an old claim - a relic attestation from months past - and add one fresh, checkable detail. A bot farm can stamp a thousand births in a night, but it cannot remember which mask signed which promise, and a wrong recall voids the whole line's standing. Cheating then grows costly like snow on a ridge: not coin, but staff-hours and the risk of exposing every old forgery at once.
